quote: In the conduct of life, habits count for more than maxims, because habit is a living maxim, become flesh and instinct. To reform one’s maxims is nothing: it is but to change the title of the book. To learn new habits is everything, for it is to reach the substance of life. Life is but a tissue of habits.
source: Henri-Frédéric Amiel, Amiel’s Journal, vol. I, pp. 7 to 8, undated thought after 30 December 1850 (trans. Mrs Humphry Ward, 1885)
note: One word corrected. Ward’s Macmillan text of 1885 reads “become flesh and instinct”; “becomes” is a slip of the American A. L. Burt reprint, which Project Gutenberg follows. The locator now rests on the preceding entry and the page, because the entry that follows is dated 16 February in 1885 and 17 February from 1888.
